newsitem.title: UK: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest-July 29.
newsitem.headline: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest-July 29.

text.p: REUTERS EMERGING EUROPE PRESS DIGEST FOR ADVERTISING & MEDIA
Weekly Press Digest from Central and Eastern Europe on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Markets
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

-- Under a new Russian law, poster advertising for alcoholic drinks must be removed from Moscow's streets and ads for alcohol will only be allowed in restaurants, bars and specific shops. The law says all posters must be removed in time for Moscow's 850th anniversary celebrations on September 4. Infringers will be fined 400-500 million roubles ($86,200). (Moskovsky Komsomolets, July 22, 1997)

-- The Czech poster union for outdoor advertising has provided 1,000 billboards free of charge for an advertising campaign to inform citizens how they can make donations to help those parts of the Czech Republic badly affected by recent floods. The ad was created by Ammirati Puris Lintas, which donated its services for free. (Strategie News, July 23-30, 1997)
-- Bulgaria's Fair Competition Commission says it will launch a six-month investigation of the country's advertising market in a move to fight unfair competition in the sector. (Pari, July 23, 1997)

-- The Czech Association of Advertising Agencies has discussed a licence agreement with the American Marketing Association to introduce the Effie advertising awards in the Czech Republic. (Strategie News, July 23-30, 1997)

-- Russian airline Aeroflot appoints advertising and public relations agency Delovaya Liga to handle part of its $100,000 advertising budget, currently held by Premier SV. (Kommersant-Daily, July 23, 1997) (Moskovsky Komsomolets, July 22, 1997)
-- Bates/Saatchi & Saatchi have been appointed to run an advertising campaign for carmaker Toyota in the Czech Republic in the autumn. (Strategie News, July 23-30, 1997)

-- Pepsi is running a poster campaign in the Czech Republic featuring super model Cindy Crawford. Andre Agassi and basketball star Shaquille O'Neal will star in future ads. The campaign is aimed primarily at teenagers. (Strategie News, July 23-30, 1997)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

-- The Sofia municipality in Bulgaria must pay 2.5 billion levs ($1.4 million) to acquire a 25 percent stake in private television station New Television, its director Mihail Mihailov says. (Capital, July 21-27, 1997)

-- New programme and management teams for Bulgarian national television and radio have been formed following Parliament's decision to replace their directors two weeks ago. (Capital, July 21-27, 1997)
-- The council for the Czech public TV station Ceska Televize has approved the network's 1997 budget. Expenditure and revenue have been set at 3.8 billion crowns. (Strategie News, July 23-30, 1997)

-- The newly established Promyana (Change) trade union branch at Bulgarian National Television says it will seek the resignation of television chiefs and leading journalists who declined to sign declarations that they had not collaborated with the communist-era secret police services. (Democratsia, July 22, 1997)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
-- Adidas is the most popular sports shoe brand in the Czech Republic, according to a survey from market researchers AISA. The second favourite is local brand Botas. (Pravo, July 22, 1997)
